lxc_43458f47469584e0.text: Imagine a giant church with a crane standing on its tower, not for a few months but for 400 years.

lxc_fdd8382b7a486d07.text: The city is also the reason we have the word "cologne" on perfume bottles.

lxc_5b46ee6457c8daf5.text: Here you will see why the cathedral waited so long, how a perfume took the city's name, and what these two stories have in common.

lxc_00394a1f7aa97853.text: Cologne Cathedral stands on a very old religious site.

lxc_c4d15ab362d55af7.text: After Roman rule ended, Merovingian kings built a church for the bishop there in the 6th century.

lxc_a80ba324068128fd.text: So when work on the Gothic cathedral began on 15 August 1248, the builders were not starting from nothing.

lxc_44d5adfeeb75aa93.text: They were adding a new chapter to a long story.

lxc_d4c87b001e30e69d.text: The people behind the project were the archbishops.

lxc_17a1f0cc095f2266.text: They built the cathedral and the city walls to present Cologne as a "Holy" city and as the capital of the land they ruled.

lxc_35575acb1e52d088.text: A huge church sent a clear message: this place matters.

lxc_f3731f3fcb895add.text: But a message like that costs money.

lxc_a04e5ebb92378243.text: Much of the early money came from pilgrims who travelled to visit the Shrine of the Three Kings.

lxc_8c4f098c92e02342.text: Think of a popular museum that pays for new rooms with ticket sales.

lxc_18a7bb08b3060c43.text: The more visitors came, the higher the stone could rise.

lxc_c581a505487d90a6.text: The eastern part, called the choir, was finished in 1322.

lxc_474c96cdf976eec7.text: Then progress slowed, and finally it stopped.

lxc_f7cb753c27946114.text: You might guess that the building was simply too hard for medieval workers.

lxc_425a8493dca8055a.text: In fact, the reasons were mostly about people and money.

lxc_0d4afcdac724e143.text: First, the city had other needs.

lxc_1ad36f9534f76ba0.text: In 1474, the craftsmen were needed to make the city's defences stronger against the Duke of Burgundy.

lxc_8411bbf39a98bff9.text: A city under threat cares more about walls than towers.

lxc_1c3b01c473c3e593.text: Second, the money began to disappear.

lxc_d1cc8a9df628100f.text: By 1473, income from pilgrims had fallen.

lxc_a346d8e44bf74157.text: Later, the Reformation and wars made things worse.

lxc_c55f5526e557663d.text: The cathedral lost its money from indulgences, which were special payments collected by the Church.

lxc_8976b322468ac7b0.text: Major work stopped in 1473 or 1474, and construction ended completely around 1560.

lxc_1a019707de8ae265.text: The clearest sign of this pause was on the south tower.

lxc_ad05aa5ffd600e1b.text: It was built only up to the level of the bells, and a large crane stayed on top of it for 400 years.

lxc_55aaf5e1879041e0.text: Generations of people in Cologne grew up looking at an unfinished building with a machine on its head.

lxc_564096a7bec0b8a6.text: The cathedral was never completely forgotten.

lxc_5257e049a649336c.text: Efforts to start again began around 1814, and work actually started again in 1823.

lxc_82c0f5b9eb81ff2c.text: Even so, proper funding arrived only in the 1840s.

lxc_4bbc4da15a995024.text: Once again, money decided the speed.

lxc_e6146db6e79dbf8d.text: The 19th-century builders made an important choice.

lxc_acdd91d6e5ad093f.text: They completed the main hall (the nave), the side arms (the transepts) and the towers by following the medieval plans.

lxc_224eccaa7cabbdb7.text: So the finished cathedral is not really a modern building pretending to be old.

lxc_5a942bd2b65226ea.text: It is closer to an old idea that waited a very long time for the money to finish it.

lxc_60a72e557b4d174a.text: People often ask why the cathedral took so long.

lxc_1c421aecf4a6cb5f.text: A better question might be: what kept the plan alive while nothing was being built?

lxc_da72a12f4a447235.text: Cologne has a second famous symbol, and this one fits in your pocket.

lxc_6c8330a446c7d68b.text: In 1709, Johann Maria Farina, an Italian, created a perfume from citrus oils and alcohol.

lxc_b83361fdd6cccba6.text: It was inspired by an Italian spring morning after rain.

lxc_f92ba24b379ad4d7.text: He named it after the city: Eau de Cologne, which means "water from Cologne".

lxc_18aa448a8ac4256d.text: The feeling of the perfume came from Italy, but its name came from a German city.

lxc_48a9270a294d8332.text: So every time someone asked for Eau de Cologne, they also said the city's name.

lxc_7d11b189bd6bf9d1.text: Famous customers helped the perfume spread.

lxc_9d6164ec00ccfd90.text: Napoleon, the writer Goethe, Queen Victoria and Empress Elisabeth all used Farina's Eau de Cologne.

lxc_644783236f677bf1.text: Napoleon reportedly used two bottles a day.

lxc_890c902577528051.text: When emperors, queens and great writers choose a product, other people want it too.

lxc_8323c52cb7914b91.text: In this way, Cologne became famous for perfume.

lxc_f5e40c542268b8b7.text: Farina's company, founded in 1709, is the world's oldest fragrance maker.

lxc_8f7970ecf0b3c284.text: Family descendants still make the original Eau de Cologne in the city.

lxc_4b8b24719464b9ce.text: Its headquarters has been in Farina House since 1723, and today that building is the Fragrance Museum, where visitors can take a 45-minute guided tour.

lxc_b2ea153edcd611eb.text: Now put the two symbols side by side.

lxc_039245a1e23713e5.text: The cathedral depended on people coming into Cologne.

lxc_757aac88096a56bc.text: Pilgrims brought money, and when that money stopped, the stones stopped too.

lxc_5f2273eec85f9491.text: The perfume worked the other way.

lxc_18b2ee4466416b88.text: It left the city in bottles and carried Cologne's name to the homes of emperors and queens.
